description.narrative: Stöd syftar till att stärka/förbättra kvaliteten och relevansen i Tanzanias nationella forskningskapacitet för att bidra till minskad fattigdom och hållbar utveckling. Mål: förbättra forskningskapacitet och dess tillämpning på största offentliga universitet i områden med natur-, samhälls- och tekniska vetenskaper, inklusive naturresurser, ingenjörvetenskap, entreprenörskap, forskningsförvaltning.

Support aims to strengthen/improve quality and relevance of the Tanzania national research capacity to contribute to poverty reduction and sustainable development. Objective: enhance research capacity and its application at the largest public university in areas of natural, social and technological sciences including, natural resources, enginnering, entrepreneurship, reserach management

General question: Results related to the intended outcome 2015Question: Summarise results related to the intended outcome (this information will be sent to Open Aid)Answer: The reporting period covers the Tanzanian fiscal year 2014/15 and this year is also the final year of the 2009-2015 year agreement for Swedish research cooperation with Tanzania. The cooperation has been extended twice with one year each time. The key objectives of the program are to promote research and research training and to develop institutional capacity in an effort to strengthen Tanzania's national research agenda as well as its national development plans to fight poverty and promote economic growth. The subject areas of research training is still highly relevant to national development goals. A total of 9 subprograms have been supported, among them 6 research training programmes in the areas of natural esources managment, marine sciences, business studies, earth sciences, renewable energy, and ural and urban infrastructure Three programmes have been focusing on support to research management and the university library providing access to scientific publications. During the year 14 PhD-students and 44 MSc-students have graduated The target was to graduate 48 PhD-students, thus there are still 34 left in the programme that will graduate after the programme has ended. The target for MSc-students was to have 58 graduates by the end of the year leaving 14 remaining students to graduate after the agreement period. There has been a positive impact with regard to the dissemination of various projects results and outputs. To date the number of publications include fifty 50 articles in international peer reviewed journals, eight (8) book chapters, six (6) international conference proceedings, nine (9) national conference proceedings, fourteen (14) PhD theses and forty four (44) MSc theses. UDSM has disseminated their results both at through locally organized conferences and workshops. For the first time this year UDSM staged the Research Week with a lot of media cover. This was instrument to UDSM becoming the winner in the category Research and Consultancy in the 2015 Sabasaba Dar es Salaam International Trade Fair. The reserach carried out on elephants use of land in western tanzanian has contributed the increase awareness of of natural resource management and more specifically through the National Elephant Day which also partially has been supported by the program. UDSM was in 2015 ranked by 4icu as number 10th best University in Africa.
